entry.title: Leave room for their reply
entry.summary: Your toddler can join a conversation through sounds, gestures, and words. Pause, listen, and respond to what they are trying to share.
entry.cue: They may point, repeat a sound, show you something, or begin a sentence.
detail: In an ordinary moment, name what you are doing or what your child notices. If you do not know the name of a bird or vehicle, you can find out together.
Give them time instead of finishing their sentence. If the meaning is unclear, invite them to show you. You can use the full word naturally in your response without making them repeat it.
Davies suggests coming to the child’s level and showing interest with your body and speech; the appendix qualifies eye contact by cultural appropriateness. Moments of silence belong in the day too.
